note: Slice c41 (Devienne, Kreusser, Förster, Cherubini): no benchmarks, no violin-catalogue overlap, no exclusion proposals. Floor evidence is mostly commercial recordings found in the Apple Music catalogue (track lists opened) and MusicBrainz; Presto and the Naxos Music Library were not reachable. Apple answered 429 once and MusicBrainz 503 once; both worked on retry. Judgement calls: (1) Cherubini's two Horn Sonatas: the IMSLP page holds only Messerschmidt's modern arrangement (horn, trumpet, euphonium) and lists one violin; the scoring (horn with string quartet) comes from the Passacaille disc and its MusicWeb review, which call them one-movement pieces; confidence medium. (2) Devienne's opus numbers collide: Op. 66 is the flute quartets (Imbault 1799), yet the Ricercar RIC416 booklet (via MusicWeb) labels three flute-violin-cello trios Op. 66/1-3 and two bassoon trios Op. 17/4-5. The three flute trios (D, G minor, C) are kept on the Imbault c. 1800 page because RISM D 1973 lists its six trios in G, G minor, C, D, F, A; they carry no opus number, 'Op. 66' is in aka, and the match rests on the keys (confidence medium; the Gaveaux page may overlap). The six Op. 17 bassoon trios (ATMA 2012) and Flute Quartet Op. 16 No. 3 (Accent 2004) are not on IMSLP. (3) Not added, scoring unverified: Devienne's Opp. 70-71 keyboard sonatas with wind and cello (Berlin Classics 1992); the Pan Classics 'String Trios Op. 39' on a Bréval & Devienne disc look like Bréval's; the 'Quartet Op. 40 No. 3' on Bongiovanni GB 5184-2 appears to be Danzi's, not Devienne's. (4) Förster: the Ensemble Les Adieux disc also holds a 'Fantasie und Sonate in D minor' of unknown scoring; Op. 21 Nos. 4-6 and Opp. 7 and 16 have modern editions but no recording or documented performance found. (5) Kreusser: gap check weak, no work list found. (6) The one outOfScope page (Devienne's Romances, Op. 53, voice with piano) is correctly out. (7) Cherubini Quartet No. 5 is dated 1835 by Wikipedia (en/de/it); IMSLP's 1825 looks like a slip.
